items.summary:
Recommendation: create no new proposals, telemetry requests, or queue admissions this cycle. Delivery is saturated at 10/10 slots; 39 deployed improvements await measurement, 21 implementation requests failed, 105 approved proposals lack execution requests, and 221 work items are stranded. The highest-leverage product opportunity is workflow hygiene: deduplicate stale work, enforce one canonical owner and next action, prevent site-overlap admission, and require every approved proposal to resolve to execution, closure, or an explicit blocker. This should be implemented only through the existing engineer queue after the current capacity gate clears.

Immediate priority: CTO completes or closes the existing saveusfarms.com repair case by 2026-10-01T09:00Z with validation, rollback, release/security, attribution, measurement, and deduplication evidence; release one slot; then admit only the existing allthingsmasonic.com CTA request. Preserve the private launch and security gates.

Product friction observed: fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no results; security and release controls remain unevidenced; task routing lacks human-triage and repeatedly falls back to nearest installed roles; validation and clean-worktree failures create repair loops; executive cycles frequently produce reports without delivery; AI usage covers only 4 of 38 expected sites; and revenue remains partially aggregated, preventing site-level ROI claims.

Ranked opportunities after capacity recovery: (1) canonical work-item lifecycle and deduplication guardrails, highest operator-time and reliability payoff, reversible and measurable by stranded-item count, duplicate-admission rate, execution rate, and cycle time; (2) release-gate failure classification and automatic repair-or-close routing, measured by failed-request recurrence and time to closure; (3) control-plane actionability view linking each approved proposal to request, owner, blocker, measurement, or closure; (4) coverage-aware AI cost and outcome review using only existing telemetry, without inventing fleet-wide cost; (5) reusable evidence-gated social and affiliate implementation contracts, measured only where existing telemetry supports it. No implementation, schedule, access, deployment, telemetry, or spend change is authorized by this recommendation.
